website.name: Mag7 Caucus
website.headline: Congress owns the Mag7
website.tagline: When multiple members of Congress disclose the same mega-cap names, that's a caucus — not a tip.
website.narrative: Mega-cap tech isn't a secret club trade — it's what shows up again and again in annual financial disclosures. Mag7 Caucus only includes AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, META, GOOGL/GOOG, and TSLA when at least two members hold them on their latest disclosed books. Weights use disclosure band midpoints with a per-person cap so one giant filing doesn't become the whole basket.
website.hook: The S&P royalty club — as disclosed on Capitol Hill.
website.rule: Ticker ∈ Mag7 (+ GOOGL); held in ≥2 latest FMP annual books; Solana catalog only; weight = band midpoint; max $5M contribution per member.
website.whyItExists: Person pages already cover individuals. This answers: which mega-caps does Congress collectively own?
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

website.name: Silicon Hill
website.headline: Tech names Congress keeps on the books
website.tagline: Not one famous portfolio — the tech stack that shows up across many disclosed books.
website.narrative: InsiderIndex already has full person trackers (including Pelosi). Silicon Hill is the opposite move: take every tradable tech single-name that appears in at least two members' latest annual disclosures, cap each member's dollar influence, and build a Hill-wide tech book. It's the collective software/semiconductor footprint of Congress — not a celebrity clone.
website.hook: Copy the committee, not the celebrity.
website.rule: Tech single-names (ex-ETFs) in ≥2 latest annual books from tech-tilted members; catalog only; band midpoints; $5M/person cap.
website.whyItExists: Avoids duplicating person pages; sells 'Congress tech exposure' as a theme.
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

website.name: Capitol Cluster
website.headline: Herd buys on the Hill
website.tagline: When 3+ members buy the same ticker, it stops looking like noise.
website.narrative: Periodic transaction reports are messy — ranges, delays, spouses. Clustering cuts through that. Capitol Cluster only keeps Solana-tradable names bought by multiple members since 2024, then equal-weights them. Filer count is the filter; equal weight keeps one mega-print from dominating.
website.rule: PTR/FMP buys since 2024-01-01; ≥3 distinct members; catalog only; equal weight.
website.whyItExists: Classic Quiver-style crowd signal, crypto-native execution path.
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

website.name: Bipartisan Handshake
website.headline: Rare agreement: both parties bought it
website.tagline: The aisle is broken — except when they buy the same stocks.
website.narrative: Party-tilt products (NANC/GOP) exaggerate differences. Handshake does the reverse: only tickers with disclosed buys from both Democrats and Republicans since 2024. Equal weight. Thin on purpose — consensus is scarce, and that's the story.
website.hook: The only bipartisan bill that clears committee.
website.rule: ≥1 Dem and ≥1 Rep buy since 2024 (strict 2/2 when universe allows); catalog; equal weight.
website.whyItExists: Political risk filter; shareable 'both sides' narrative.
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

website.name: Fresh Ink
website.headline: Newest Congressional buy prints
website.tagline: Sized by disclosure band midpoints — the loudest recent ink on the tape.
website.narrative: The feed is for copying one print. Fresh Ink is for scanning many: recent buy disclosures, ranked by dollar-band midpoints, capped to the top 20 Solana-tradable names. It's a research basket that feels like the news cycle.
website.rule: Buys ≥2024-06-01 (undated kept); catalog; weight ∝ band midpoint; top 20.
website.whyItExists: Bridges /feed urgency into an index ticket.

website.name: Beta Caucus
website.headline: Congress buys the market itself
website.tagline: VOO, IVV, QQQ — the quiet wealth stack hiding in financial disclosures.
website.narrative: Not every story is NVDA. A surprising share of disclosed books is index ETFs. Beta Caucus gathers members with ≥3 catalog ETF holdings and weights those ETF legs by disclosure midpoints. It's the 'adults in the room' basket — boring on purpose, and that's the joke.
website.hook: The most bipartisan trade: own the market.
website.rule: Members with ≥3 catalog ETF legs; constituents=those ETFs; band midpoints; $3M/person cap.
website.whyItExists: Contrasts meme-tech with how Congress actually indexes.

website.name: Whip's Desk
website.headline: Banks, brokers, cards on the books
website.tagline: The finance names that survive committee markup — and annual filings.
website.narrative: Financial Services is the most common 'top sector' tag on PelosiTracker hitters. Whip's Desk isolates catalog-tradable banks, brokers, and cards from finance-tilted disclosed books. It's power-broker aesthetics without cloning any single member.
website.rule: Finance single-names from finance-tagged / ≥2-finance-holding members; prefer tickers held by ≥2; catalog; band midpoints; $2M/person cap.
website.whyItExists: Sector story with liquid, familiar tickers.
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

website.name: Capitol Arsenal
website.headline: Defense & aerospace on disclosure forms
website.tagline: Prime contractors and aerospace names that appear in Congressional books.
website.narrative: Defense committees make headlines; disclosed holdings make this index. Capitol Arsenal collects Solana-tradable aerospace/defense names from the latest annual books across the roster. Sparse by design — when the set is thin, that honesty is part of the product.
website.rule: Defense/aerospace tickers in latest annual books; catalog only; band midpoints; $2M/person cap.
website.whyItExists: Geopolitics narrative; distinct from tech/finance clones.
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

website.name: Dual Lock
website.headline: Still held. Still buying.
website.tagline: Annual book + fresh purchase — double confirmation, no celebrity required.
website.narrative: A buy print can be noise. A position on the annual form can be stale. Dual Lock requires both: the ticker is on a member's latest disclosed book and appears in their 2024+ buy tape. Prefer names locked by ≥2 members. Equal weight.
website.rule: Intersection of latest catalog holdings and 2024+ buys; prefer ≥2 members; equal weight.
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

website.name: House Heat
website.headline: What Congress can't stop buying
website.tagline: A social heat list — ranked by raw purchase count, equal weight.
website.narrative: Ignore dollar bands for a second. Sometimes the story is frequency: which tickers keep showing up on purchase disclosures. House Heat ranks by buy count since 2024, takes the top 15 catalog names, and equal-weights. Built for share cards and weekly refresh.
website.rule: Top 15 catalog tickers by 2024+ buy count; equal weight.
website.whyItExists: Social/virality surface distinct from midpoint-weighted Fresh Ink.
website.sourceLine: Sources: House Clerk / Senate eFD filings via FMP; member context via PelosiTracker; tradability via InsiderIndex Solana catalog (xStocks + Backpack .US).

disclaimers: Not investment advice. Public disclosures are delayed (STOCK Act allows up to ~45 days) and often report dollar ranges, not exact fills.
Model indexes are research presentations of disclosed activity. They are not NAV, not audited performance, and not a brokerage product.
InsiderIndex does not claim members of Congress endorse these baskets.
Copying a single disclosure print (user-signed swap) is separate from holding a model index.
Return and hit-rate metrics stay blank until a real dated price series is wired — we do not invent alpha.
